bugs: Marking a task done without setting completed_at leaves it out of tasks_completed_last_7_days (confirmed with a probe). Nothing keeps status and completed_at in sync.
antipatterns: app/Services/TeamDashboardCache.php:20-38 hand-rolls stale-while-revalidate with a lock, a 'last' key and versioning instead of Cache::flexible. Stale data is only served when the lock is contended, so a cache that expires after 300s is always rebuilt in the request.
app/Services/TeamDashboardCache.php:36 falls back to computing synchronously when the lock times out and no 'last' entry exists, so lock waiters can still stampede.
app/Services/TeamDashboardCache.php:59-67 creates the version with Str::random plus add/get, where an add+increment integer counter would be simpler.
tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:12-17 fakeHttp() calls Http::swap(new Factory) to reset stubs, which is test ceremony.
tests/Feature/DashboardTest.php:95-115 dataset closures take positional ($t, $project, $task, $teammate) arguments, which makes the cases hard to read.
app/Services/*: two service classes (ExchangeRateClient and ExchangeRates) plus a separate BuildTeamDashboard invokable is a lot of layering for this task.
strengths: The UserObserver also invalidates member_count when a user joins, leaves or is deleted. All observers implement ShouldHandleEventsAfterCommit and handle a project or task moving to another team (old and new team are both invalidated).
Version-key invalidation means a rebuild that was already running cannot write old data under the new key, and a test proves it.
The dashboard rebuild and the rate refresh both take a lock and re-check the cache inside it. A 30s cooldown after a failed API call and a 30-day last-known key cover the stale and 503 requirements.
The Http client sets connectTimeout and a timeout from config, uses baseUrl, and calls throw(). Empty or garbage bodies are treated as failures.

The lock wait is injectable, so the lock-contention tests run instantly without sleeping. The suite covers 43 cases, including lock contention, cooldown, a dataset of error statuses, travel() past the TTLs and both teams on a move.
Thin invokable controllers use the `?? abort()` idiom, the FormRequest normalises to uppercase and has a typed accessor, and the models use #[Scope], #[ObservedBy] and #[Fillable].

bugs: member_count is not invalidated when a user joins or leaves a team, because there is no User observer. A probe confirmed the dashboard keeps showing the old count for up to 60s fresh plus up to 300s stale. The task only requires projects and tasks to show up within seconds, so this is minor.

The first request after an invalidation finds an empty versioned key, and Cache::flexible computes on a cold miss with no lock. Concurrent requests after every write therefore all recompute (a stampede).
antipatterns: app/Observers/TaskObserver.php:15-21 hides domain state logic (setting completed_at) in a 'saving' hook on an observer marked ShouldHandleEventsAfterCommit, which mixes concerns. It worked in a probe inside a transaction, but it is fragile and surprising.

app/Support/FetchExchangeRates.php:21-25 hardcodes the timeout and lock wait as constants, so they cannot be injected or configured. As a result tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:113-125 really blocks for 4 seconds.
app/Support/FetchExchangeRates.php:62 sets no connectTimeout and does no acceptJson/baseUrl setup, only the URL in config.
bootstrap/app.php: redirectGuestsTo('/login') points at a route that does not exist. It works only because API errors render as JSON.
The ExampleTest from the base was left in place.
strengths: Cache::flexible([60, 300]) is the idiomatic fit for 'stale for up to 5 minutes is acceptable', combined with version-key invalidation (add+increment) so writes show up immediately.
Team::tasks() HasManyThrough keeps the dashboard queries expressive.
The ExchangeRatesUnavailable exception has its own render() method, so the controller stays a single line.
The rate lookup takes a lock with block() and re-checks the cache inside it, uses a cooldown after failures, keeps a separate last-known key, and returns 503 when nothing is known.
The saving hook stamps or clears completed_at, so status and completed_at stay consistent.
There are fewer files and less ceremony overall.
The tests cover the timeout via a ConnectionException, malformed bodies, the cooldown and its retry, and lock contention.

v.rationale:
Both test suites pass: impl-1 runs 43 tests and impl-2 runs 31. I probed each with throwaway tests and then deleted them. For impl-1 I checked invalidation inside a transaction (passes), a non-array 'rates' body (returns 503) and the TTL window (passes). The one gap was that marking a task done without completed_at is not counted. For impl-2 I checked the completed_at stamp inside a transaction (passes), invalidation inside a transaction (passes), Cache::flexible serving stale data and then refreshing (passes) and a non-JSON guest getting 401 (passes). The one gap was that member_count stays out of date after a user joins.

impl-2 has the more idiomatic caching core: Cache::flexible with version-bump invalidation is close to what the task describes, and it is simpler. However, it does not invalidate on member changes, has no stampede protection on the cold miss after each invalidation, hardcodes the timeouts so one test sleeps for 4 seconds, and puts domain logic in an observer's saving hook.

impl-1 hand-rolls the stale-while-revalidate behaviour, which is more ceremony than Cache::flexible, and it only serves stale data when another request holds the lock. In return it is more complete and more robust. It has a lock around the dashboard rebuild, invalidates on member changes, sets connectTimeout and a configurable timeout, and makes the lock wait injectable. Its tests are much more thorough: a mid-computation race, lock contention, a dataset of API error statuses, and both teams being invalidated when a project moves.

On balance, impl-1's completeness and test quality outweigh impl-2's neater use of the framework, so impl-1 ranks first by a small margin.
